digest.headline: Seven weeks, a new frontier: Claude Opus 5.5 tops the AA index, GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches Astra at a fifth of the price, Gemini 4 Argon arrives gated, and Pi hits 1.0
digest.summary: This is the first refresh since August 17, and a lot has happened. OpenAI shipped GPT-6 Astra (Sep 3), then GPT-6 Sol (Sep 22) and GPT-6.1 Sol (Sep 29). The 6.1 Sol release lands one point behind Astra on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at $2/$10. Anthropic answered with Claude Opus 5.5 on Sep 22: Fable-class capability, 40% cheaper to run than Opus 5, and the new #1 on AA's index at 58 (v4.3). Sonnet 5.5 followed on Sep 28 at 56. xAI's 2.1T-parameter Grok 4.7 landed mid-pack at 46. Google announced Gemini 4 Argon on Sep 30 but is limiting access to cyber defenders for now. On policy, President Trump created a White House 'Super Intelligence Force' led by DNI Jay Clayton after AI labs signed voluntary safety commitments. Anthropic disclosed a Claude-powered influence-for-hire operation targeting Malaysian voters, and OpenAI began watermarking ChatGPT text in the EU. Tooling: Pi reached 1.0 with fullscreen-by-default and leaner codemode, Claude Code added Claude Mods, and Codex is on 0.160.1. Because AA moved to Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, the model board has been rebuilt on the current scales.

stories.title: Claude Opus 5.5 ships at Fable-class capability for 40% less than Opus 5
stories.dek: Released September 22, Opus 5.5 is the first model in Anthropic's 5.5 family. It's priced at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens (20% below Opus 5), generates more than 30% faster, and has a 1M-token context with 128K max output. Artificial Analysis measured 58 on its Intelligence Index at max effort, the highest score it has recorded. That figure drops to 42 at low effort, so the effort dial matters. Thinking can't be disabled, and default effort is now medium. It's Anthropic's first release since it called for pacing the frontier, and external evaluators including METR tested it before launch.
stories.whyItMatters: It retakes the top of the independent leaderboard while cutting the price. The 16-point spread across effort levels also means that comparing models without matching effort settings is now close to meaningless.

stories.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches GPT-6 Astra at one-fifth the price
stories.dek: GPT-6.1 Sol arrived September 29, just seven days after GPT-6 Sol, which it replaces. OpenAI says it matches GPT-6 Astra on DeepSWE v1.1 at roughly a fifth of the cost, priced at $2/$10 per million tokens with $0.10 cached input and a 1.05M context. Prompts over 272K input tokens are billed at higher rates. Artificial Analysis puts it at 52 on its Intelligence Index, one point below Astra (53). It's live in the API, ChatGPT, and Codex.
stories.whyItMatters: Astra-level agentic coding at Sonnet-tier prices makes GPT-6.1 Sol the obvious default in Codex. That leaves Astra as a specialist for security and bio-reasoning work.

stories.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5 closes in on Opus at half the price
stories.dek: Anthropic's Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) launched September 28 at $2/$10 per million tokens, unchanged from Sonnet 5. Anthropic says it's 30%+ faster and up to 30% cheaper per task than its predecessor. It scores 56 on the AA Intelligence Index and 55.5% on CursorBench 4.0, second only to Opus 5.5 on both.
stories.whyItMatters: Mid-tier models now sit within a couple of points of the flagship, so routing most agent work to Sonnet and escalating only hard cases to Opus is now an easy call.

stories.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon, but access goes to cyber defenders first
stories.dek: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on September 30. It's aimed at software engineering, enterprise knowledge work, and cybersecurity defense, with an industry-leading 1M-token output limit. Introductory pricing is $2/$10 per million tokens, rising to $4/$20 later. It's rolling out first to trusted defenders in Google's Fairwind Program, with paid API and AI Ultra access to follow and no general-availability date yet.
stories.whyItMatters: Google is copying the gated, defenders-first rollout pattern for capable cyber models. The model also has no independent benchmark scores yet, so it isn't on the board.

stories.title: xAI's Grok 4.7 grows to 2.1T parameters but lands mid-pack
stories.dek: Grok 4.7 shipped September 21 with 2.1 trillion parameters (up 40% from Grok 4.6) and longer RL training, at an unchanged $2/$6 per million tokens. It scores 46 on AA Intelligence Index v4.3, up 2 points from Grok 4.6 but well behind Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra at 53. It hits only 26% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, against 60% for Astra. On CursorBench 4.0 it posts 46.3%, roughly level with Claude Opus 5.
stories.whyItMatters: Scaling parameters alone didn't keep xAI in the top tier this cycle. Grok's case now rests on price and Cursor-style coding, not frontier intelligence.

stories.title: Trump creates a White House 'Super Intelligence Force' led by DNI Jay Clayton
stories.dek: Announced October 4, the task force includes FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson, the Pentagon's Emil Michael, and OPM Director Scott Kupor, and reports to the President and Chief of Staff Susie Wiles. It follows a White House meeting where OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, and SpaceXAI signed voluntary safety standards with 'four layers of controls and audits': internal evals, external audits, and board reviews. Trump called the standards 'morally binding.'
stories.whyItMatters: It's the clearest sign yet of US AI governance: federal coordination plus industry self-regulation, rather than binding legislation.

stories.title: Anthropic exposes a Claude-powered influence-for-hire operation targeting Malaysian voters
stories.dek: Anthropic's September threat-intelligence report describes an operation that fed census and electoral data into Claude to micro-target constituencies. It ran roughly 1,000 fake X accounts with 'warm-up' logic, a fake news site called 'Malaysia Pulse,' and fabricated dossiers, and the actors used Claude Code to build a sock-puppet monitoring dashboard. The report attributes the platform to Istanbul-based BBS Bilisim Teknolojileri, which sold it as 'influence-as-a-service.' Anthropic saw no signs that it gained significant traction.
stories.whyItMatters: Coding agents are now part of the influence-op toolchain, not just content generators. That widens what labs have to monitor for misuse.

stories.title: OpenAI starts invisibly watermarking ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU
stories.dek: OpenAI's textGrain embeds a statistical signal in word choice, using a secret key to pick among equally good words, with no hidden characters. It's rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex output in the EU to comply with Article 50 of the EU AI Act. API customers worldwide can opt in from October 5; it's off by default. Detection is about 80% at 200 tokens and 95% at 400, but swapping 25% of words for synonyms drops it to 17%.
stories.whyItMatters: Regulation, not voluntary policy, is what pushed OpenAI to ship text watermarking. Light paraphrasing defeats it, though, so it's a compliance signal, not a reliable detector.

modelsMeta.note: Board rebuilt October 5. Since the last refresh, Artificial Analysis moved to Intelligence Index v4.3 and CursorBench to 4.0, both on much lower absolute scales (Claude Opus 5 went from 61 to 51 on AA). So every row now uses the current versions; the old numbers aren't comparable. New this cycle: Claude Opus 5.5 (the new AA #1 at 58), Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6.1 Sol, and Grok 4.7. Grok 4.6's AA score is derived from AA's statement that Grok 4.7 scored +2 over it. DeepSWE figures come from BenchLM's aggregation (last updated Sep 1), plus Opus 5.5's 74.2 from BenchLM's head-to-head. Gemini 4 Argon is not listed yet because it has no independent scores. Older models no longer near the frontier (Opus 4.8, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Flash) were dropped because they lack v4.3 / CursorBench 4.0 scores.

harness.notes: 2.1.287 (Oct 1) added Claude Mods, which let plugins modify deeper harness behavior, plus a built-in 'You should know' mod (`/plugin enable cc-plugin-you-should-know@builtin`), an `n:<text>` filter in the agents view, and URL prompts from MCP servers. 2.1.288 added `--max-findings <n>|all` to /code-review, a built-in `gh api` for cloud sessions without the GitHub CLI, recovery of Ctrl+C-cleared prompts with Up, a re-auth prompt when MCP servers ask for more OAuth scope, and fixes for mid-response API timeouts and 'Prompt is too long' during auto-compact. 2.1.289 fixed deny/ask rules on nested compound shell commands and Read deny rules bypassed through symlinked @-mentions, and added `agent.spawn` for teammates.

0.160.0 (Oct 1) added a 'Show more' action for older tasks in the agent command center, sessions started outside a project with workspace defaults, opt-in Guardian review context (earlier user instructions and agent handoffs), and middle-click paste on Linux X11. It also fixed duplicate sends after reconnects, subagent environment handoff, and SQLite stalls, and caches plugin manifests. 0.160.1 backports a fix that preserves SYSTEMROOT/TEMP/TMP for remote stdio MCP servers on Windows executors. GPT-6.1 Sol is now available in Codex.

Pi hit 1.0 on October 1. The TUI is now fullscreen by default (`tuiMode: "regular"` restores scrollback), codemode uses about 40% fewer prompt tokens and gives errors that tell the model how to recover, and scripts can generate images via `models.generateImages()`. 1.0 also adds Radius sign-in plus MCP setup and hardens MCP OAuth (RFC 9207 `iss` checks, per-server credentials). 1.0.1 added a Nix flake, per-project MCP overrides in `.pi/mcp.json`, and CIMD OAuth client registration. 1.0.2 added `samplingParamsByThinkingLevel`. 1.0.3 adds Azure Foundry Chat Completions and is BREAKING: the provider `azure-openai-responses` was renamed to `azure`, so update auth.json, models.json, and settings.json.

extensions.name: AWS MCP Server
extensions.blurb: AWS's managed MCP server gives coding agents one interface to AWS APIs for provisioning, inspecting, and troubleshooting workloads, with no per-service integrations. On October 2 it expanded to six more regions (Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, Ireland, London, Oregon), eight in total, so teams can keep request data in-region.

extensions.name: Radius MCP (via Pi 1.0)
extensions.blurb: Pi 1.0's `/login` offers 'Sign in with Radius' and then configures the Radius MCP server in your global `mcp.json` with `"auth": { "provider": "radius" }` in one step. It's a good example of identity-provider login and MCP server setup collapsing into a single flow.

extensions.name: Stateless MCP on Cloudflare Workers
extensions.blurb: Cloudflare's guide to the 2026-07-28 MCP spec: servers can run 'in just a Worker' with no stateful infrastructure. Multi round-trip requests replace stream-based elicitation, `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers let gateways and WAFs inspect traffic, and Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated in favor of pre-registered clients. Pi 1.0.1's CIMD support and Claude Code's scope step-up prompts are clients catching up to this.

tips.title: Stop telling Opus 5.5 to 'think carefully'
tips.body: Opus 5.5 sets its own thinking budget on every reply, and thinking can't be turned off, so 'think hard'-style phrases add nothing. Instead, put the whole task and a clear finish line in one message. For long runs, keep the task list in a file like TASKS.md so it survives context summarization. Default effort is now medium. Raise it deliberately when results fall short; Artificial Analysis measured a 16-point index spread between low and max.

tips.title: Cap or uncap /code-review findings
tips.body: Claude Code 2.1.288 added `--max-findings <n>|all` to /code-review. Use a small number for a quick pre-commit pass that surfaces only the top issues, or `all` before a big merge when you want every finding. The same release lets you recover a prompt you cleared with Ctrl+C: press Up to bring the draft back.

tips.title: Turn a global MCP server off for just one project
tips.body: Pi 1.0.1 supports project overrides for user-level MCP servers. Add an entry to `.pi/mcp.json` with no `command` or `url`, setting only `enabled`, `exposure`, or `toolExposure`, or toggle it from `/mcp`. That keeps a noisy or sensitive server out of one repo's sessions without touching your global config.
